#+TITLE: Measurement Apparatus — ablation runner, multi-stage oracle on the driver seam, z-profile probe, ablation.json, CI
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: measurement-apparatus

* Summary

The measurement doctrine is already written into plan 006: *no algorithm deltas before the measurement apparatus exists* — the current oracle (test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp: 3 Kneel_1 frames, trunk-only, flat budget 3000, backface OFF, IoU ≥ 0.85) cannot see the z-weak axis, and DIRECT numeric convergence is too noisy for raw-pose gates (docs/plans/2026-08-11-006-refactor-shared-vm-layer-extraction-plan.md "Follow-On Optimization Phase"). This angle specs the apparatus in four instruments that reuse existing seams rather than new infrastructure: (1) a headless Tier-0 CPU metric reference (the per-metric semantics that 02 pins, consumed as test-only math); (2) a manifest-driven Tier-2 GPU ablation runner over the 7 registered cost variants × budget shapes × dilation schedules, writing test/golden/ablation.json; (3) a z-profile probe that sweeps z_trans through the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+) — the cheapest instrument that can see the z-weak axis; (4) a production-shaped multi-stage oracle (20k→25k→30k→35k cumulative, per-stage dilation, tibia-after-femur, sym_trap) driven through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam with appearance-only gates (per-frame IoU ≥ 0.85, per-px L1 and z recorded against baseline.json bands), plus a CI shape (new gpu label, self-hosted RTX 3090 runner, data-profile-reduced per-PR budget) that leaves the headless suite untouched.

* Key Findings

** The ablation runner is a two-tier split: a headless CPU metric reference (Tier-0) and a GPU per-variant scorer (Tier-2), joined by a manifest — never hand-written per-variant tests
- Tier-0 (headless, CI, CPU): reference implementations of the metric semantics — overlap count + comparison-white-sum normalization (FastImplantDilationMetric), mean-chamfer on the L1 distance map (DistanceMapMetric), IoU, L1,1, Mahfouz intensity ratio — on synthetic binary images, in test/unit/. The headless Frame twin already provides edge/dilation/distance-map via pure OpenCV (test/unit/frame_headless.cpp implements Canny/dilate/invert/distanceTransform against the same include/compute/frame.h), so every input the metrics consume is producible CPU-side. The metric contracts are documented in include/compute/gpu_metrics.cuh (IOU = intersection/union of white spaces; L_1_1 = summed abs diff; FastImplantDilationMetric = overlap normalized by the comparison white-pixel sum). These are test-only reference implementations (R13: no production edits); 02-cost-path-foundation owns the per-metric semantics tests and this tier consumes them.
- Tier-2 (GPU, gpu label): run each variant on Kneel_1 (3 frames) under the production budget shape with the oracle's appearance gate (silhouette IoU ≥ 0.85 vs Labels/fem — independent of all cost math; the R2 guardrail "never validate a metric by its own optimum"). Record recovered pose per axis, IoU, per-px L1, z-gap vs fem.jts, and cost-call count into ablation.json. The compute-only shape (DirectOptimizer bound to the real GPU cost, exactly oracle_test.cpp's BuildFramePipeline + cost lambda pattern) is the Tier-2 workhorse; the app-wiring shape is the multi-stage oracle below.
- Per-variant configuration surface (the matrix the manifest must encode): variant name ∈ the 7 registered costs (CostFunctionManager::listCostFunctions: sym_trap_function, DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_SAME_Z, DIRECT_DILATION_T1, DIRECT_DILATION, DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423); per-stage budget shape (production 20000/5000/5000/5000 cumulative 20k→25k→30k→35k, reduced data-profile shape, flat 3000 oracle shape — baseline.json budget_per_stage/budget_cumulative_effective); per-stage dilation schedule (6/3/1 per golden_oracle.org prose vs 6/4/1 per TRUNK_DILATION 6 + BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE 2 + Z_SEARCH_DILATION 1 in include/domain/settings_constants.h — the contradiction is itself an ablation axis; each variant's own registered Dilation int param per src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp); ranges (trunk ±35, branch (15,15,25,25,25,25), leaf (3,3,15,3,3,3) — settings_constants.h); backface ON (production) vs OFF (oracle/label-generator); frame set {0,1,2}.
- Cost profile that makes this tractable: the flat-3000 oracle run takes "a few minutes" on the RTX 3090 (qml_parity_check.cpp kRunTimeoutMs = 30 min watchdog) ⇒ roughly 20–60 evals/s ⇒ the 35k production shape is ~10–30 min/frame, and the full matrix (7 variants × 3 frames × production shape) is hours — which is why the manifest is required (selectable subsets), a reduced shape is CI-default, and the full shape is nightly. [Source: repo — test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp, test/oracle/qml_parity_check.cpp:124-126, test/golden/baseline.json, src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423, test/unit/frame_headless.cpp, include/compute/gpu_metrics.cuh]
- Confidence: high (repo-internal, source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: this is the missing decision tool — the 7 registered variants have never been compared head-to-head (test/unit/test_cost_function.cpp covers only the parameter registry), and every algorithm claim in the run's papers (DIRECT-GLh hidden constraints, refinement control) needs this harness before it can be judged.

** The multi-stage oracle drives the REAL Optimize() stage loop through the OptimizerRunDriver seam — OptimizerRunLaunch is the payload, the controller relays are the observation channel, and the gates stay appearance-based
- The seam is ready and green: include/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.h defines OptimizerRunLaunch (calibration, camera_a/b frames, models, selected_model_indexes, primary_model_index, pose_matrix LocationStorage, OptimizerSettings, the three CostFunctionManagers by value, directive, iter_count) and the OptimizerRunDriver interface (Manager/ThreadActive/Initialize/Start/Stop/Wait) with the production adapter CreateOptimizerManagerRunDriver wrapping OptimizerManager untouched (src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp: a fresh manager + QThread per run, finished-before-Initialize bind, H3 destructor contract). OptimizerRunController::start() drives the sequence (save-last-pose mirror → gate → seed → driver → 8 binds → Initialize → thread start) and re-emits by-value relays on the controller thread; the core exposes the oracle seam's observation channel directly: costCalls(), stageText(), progress() (optimizer_run_controller_core.h:154-165, "calls vs cumulative budget — the oracle seam, M12").
- What the oracle must therefore do: construct OptimizerRunRequest{ directive, save-last-pose mirror args, gate inputs, LocationStorage seeded from fem.jts frame 0, launch{ production OptimizerSettings, three CFMs with DIRECT_DILATION + per-stage dilation params, frames built at Canny 3/0/150 + dilation 6, models = femur (primary) + tibia (non-principal) } }, call start(), wait for runState == Completed, then run the appearance comparator (GPUModel backface OFF + GPUMetrics::IOU vs the vertically-flipped label TIFF — the exact oracle mechanics) at the pose relayed by optimizedFrameRelayed. The real stage loop runs unmodified inside OptimizerManager::Optimize(): trunk budget 20000 → 2×branch 5000 each (budget_ accumulates 25k/30k) → leaf 5000 (35k), each stage a fresh DirectOptimizer with SetCallOffset(cost_function_calls_) so the loop guard is cumulative (optimizer_manager.cpp:1031, 1087-1093, 1142-1146; DirectOptimizer::SetCallOffset in include/domain/direct_optimizer.h), per-stage re-dilate of the comparison image to the stage's dilation value, and per-stage CFM Initialize/Destruct.
- The gates (per baseline.json tolerances): (a) HARD — per-frame silhouette IoU ≥ 0.85 vs the empirically pinned label (baseline.json silhouette_iou_threshold; measured 0.9936 — the IoU gate stays the appearance arbiter, never raw pose); (b) BANDED-RECORD — per-px L1 vs the baseline 0.021 informational threshold (measured 0.0207; promote to a banded assert only after the cross-GPU noise floor is calibrated — prior-run angle 06 finding, https://www.forasoft.com/learn/video-quality/articles-vqm/regression-testing-golden-references); (c) BANDED-INFORMATIONAL — z-gap vs baseline.json pose_per_axis_informational z_tran = 15.0 (observed 6.31) — recorded per frame into ablation.json and asserted only inside the band, because DIRECT z convergence is noisy by design; (d) STAGE-BOOKKEEPING — the controller's costCalls() at each stage transition must land on the cumulative caps 20k/25k/30k/35k (± the seed eval), and per-stage CFM Dilation parameters must match the manifest — this is the regression the flat-3000 oracle is blind to (a SetCallOffset or dilation-scheduling regression passes today).
- Tibia-after-femur + sym_trap: the production workflow is sequential runs — femur as primary (tibia pinned non-principal from tib.jts via LocationStorage, which Optimize() reads for the pole/sym_trap costs at optimizer_manager.cpp:937-947), then tibia as primary with the femur pose fixed at the recovered value. The QML bridge's SingleModelOnly pre-check would reject the two-model launch, so the oracle drives OptimizerRunController directly (the widgets' full surface), not the bridge stack — qml_parity_check.cpp remains the proven harness template for the single-model case. The Sym_Trap string directive (optimizer_manager.cpp:177-185 → CalculateSymTrap) is NOT in the controller's typed Directive enum (Single/All/Each/From/… — optimizer_run_controller_core.h:58-62), so the tibia-ambiguity pass needs a small seam addition (a typed Directive::SymTrap mapped to the manager string) — the one concrete seam gap this spec found.
- Confidence: high (repo-internal, source-verified; the seam behavior is pinned by the green jtml.optimizer_run_controller lifecycle suite per the plan-006 record)
- Relevance: this is synthesis roadmap item 3 (production-shaped multi-stage oracle) — the highest-leverage expansion, and the acceptance test for any future shared-stage-loop refactor (plan 006 explicitly shapes the run controller as its future seam: "the multi-stage oracle consumes the OptimizerRunDriver seam from U5").

** The z-profile probe reuses the RunDirectStage injected-cost boundary — sweep z_trans with all other axes pinned at fem.jts truth and read the cost curve; it is the cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis
- The entry point is optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+ — RunDirectStage's injected lambda takes the denormalized physical Point6D, sets the GPU model pose (primary + biplane secondary via calibration convert), and scores stage_manager.callActiveCostFunction(). The probe replicates exactly that lambda body (or, for the driver-seam variant, drives a controller run with leaf-like settings), looping Δz ∈ {-15,-14,…,+15} mm around the fem.jts z at fixed truth for the other 5 axes, recording cost(Δz) per variant per dilation level.
- Why it exposes the z-weak-axis signal directly: the dilated-overlap family is nearly flat in z because a z shift is pure magnification — at ~1.1 m source distance a ±15 mm shift changes scale by <1%, inside the 6 px dilation tolerance — so the probe's diagnostic is the normalized depth of the cost valley: valley_depth = (max_{Δz} cost − cost(0)) / (max − min over the sweep). A healthy z signal shows a deep, centered valley; a z-blind metric shows a flat curve (or worse, an off-center one). Per-variant ranking (chamfer-heavy DIRECT_DILATION ≥ Mahfouz ≥ pure overlap) is exactly what this instrument measures — prior-run angle 01 hypothesis (repo .panoptes/jtml-research-horizons/angles/01-cost-function-landscape.org, the magnification arithmetic derived from baseline.json z_tran ≈ -1022.93 and pitch 0.373).
- Cost: 31 cost calls per (variant, dilation, frame) ≈ 31 renders — milliseconds each at ~20-60 evals/s ⇒ the whole 7-variant × 3-dilation × 3-frame probe is on the order of a couple of minutes on the RTX 3090. It needs no production changes (the boundary already exists) and no new fixtures. As a metamorphic-relation bonus it asserts cheap oracle-quality invariants: cost(0) is the sweep minimum within noise, and valley depth > a noise floor — a variant that fails this is z-blind by measurement, not by argument.
- Headless Tier-0 analog: the CPU metric reference can run the same sweep on synthetic silhouettes scaled by the magnification factor, giving a no-GPU z-sensitivity estimate; the GPU probe remains authoritative because it exercises the real render + metric path (this is 05-compute-perf's boundary: the probe consumes timing, it does not own instrumentation).
- Confidence: high on the probe mechanics (the lambda boundary is source-verified); medium on the per-variant valley-depth ranking until the probe runs (it is a measurement instrument by design, not a claim).
- Relevance: the z-weak axis is the run's load-bearing research problem (prior-run synthesis finding, converged from 5 independent literature sources + the 6.31 mm measured z gap); this probe is the instrument that turns the argument into data and gates every z remedy (SAME_Z weight calibration, chamfer reweighting, leaf refinement).

** ablation.json schema — variant × budget shape × dilation schedule × metric → per-frame IoU / per-px L1 / z-gap, plus the run hash (determinism record)
- Concrete schema (test/golden/ablation.json, sibling of baseline.json):
  #+begin_example
  {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "runner": {
      "gpu": "RTX 3090", "cuda": "12.4", "timestamp": "...",
      "run_hash": "sha256(variant|budget_shape|dilation_schedule|frames|start_pose_source|backface|edge_config)"
    },
    "variants": [
      {
        "name": "DIRECT_DILATION",
        "cost_path": "src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp",
        "params": {"Dilation": 6, "Black_Silhouette": null},
        "dilation_schedule": {"trunk": 6, "branch": 3, "leaf": 1},
        "budget_cumulative": [20000, 25000, 30000, 35000],
        "ranges": {"trunk": [35,35,35,35,35,35], "branch": [15,15,25,25,25,25], "leaf": [3,3,15,3,3,3]},
        "backface": false,
        "edge_config": {"canny": [3, 0, 150]},
        "results": [
          {"frame": 0, "recovered_pose": [x,y,z,xa,ya,za],
           "iou": 0.9936, "l1_per_px": 0.0207, "z_gap_mm": 6.31,
           "cost_calls": 35000, "elapsed_s": 1234.0,
           "gate": {"iou_pass": true, "l1_band_pass": true, "z_band_pass": true}}
        ],
        "determinism": {"seeds": [], "note": "no RNG in DIRECT or the int-atomic cost path; run_hash is the determinism twin",
                        "re_runs_identical": true}
      }
    ],
    "z_profiles": [
      {"variant": "DIRECT_DILATION", "dilation": 6, "frame": 0,
       "sweep_mm": [-15,-14,...,15], "costs": [ ... ],
       "valley_depth_norm": 0.42, "argmin_mm": 1.0}
    ]
  }
  #+end_example
- Determinism semantics (the seeds column is honest about being empty today): DIRECT is RNG-free (pure convex-hull/trisection bookkeeping — src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp) and every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd, which is order-independent and therefore value-deterministic run-to-run on a machine (prior-run angle 05 finding; the only float-atomic reduction, render_drr_engine.cu's DRR fill, is not in the DIRECT cost path). So the determinism twin is: same run_hash ⇒ bit-identical output on the same GPU; the runner asserts it by running the flagship variant twice. The seeds array is reserved for future stochastic variants (e.g., multistart) and for cross-GPU noise-floor trials.
- The run_hash (not a seed) is the schema's regression tripwire: any change to variant/budget/dilation/frame-set/start-pose-source/backface/edge-config that forgets to update the manifest changes the hash and fails the diff review.
- Confidence: high (schema is a proposal grounded in the verified repo fields: baseline.json's budget_cumulative_effective/tolerances/measured block is the template; the 7 variants' registered params are source-verified)
- Relevance: ablation.json is the decision record the harness produces — the per-variant z-gap table is what the DIRECT variant switch (01-direct-variants) and the weight calibrations (02) get judged against; it lives next to baseline.json so the golden spec and the ablation data are one directory.

** CI integration — a new gpu ctest label, a self-hosted RTX 3090 runner, a data-profile-reduced per-PR budget shape, and nightly full shape; the headless suite is untouched by construction
- Current state: the headless suite is `ctest -L headless` (pixi.toml test task, --timeout 600) and is the only thing GitHub Actions runs (workflows/cmake.yml); GPU tests carry labels "oracle" (TIMEOUT 3600) and "oracle;render" (TIMEOUT 120) and are never in the default run — the split is already load-bearing. New tests must follow the same registration recipe (repo-root WORKING_DIRECTORY, xcb env for renderers, explicit labels).
- New targets and labels:
  - jtml.metric_reference — Tier-0 CPU metric reference + z-profile Tier-0 analog. LABELS "headless", TIMEOUT 120-300. Zero GPU, zero impact on the existing 46 headless tests beyond a new green target.
  - jtml.z_profile — GPU probe. LABELS "gpu;oracle", TIMEOUT 600 (a couple of minutes of renders). This is the per-PR z-health check.
  - jtml.ablation — manifest-driven runner. LABELS "gpu", TIMEOUT sized to the manifest's budget shape (reduced shape ≤ 30 min per PR; the full production shape is NOT a ctest case — it is a nightly job with a job-level timeout, because 7 variants × 3 frames × 35k evals is hours).
  - jtml.oracle_multistage — the driver-seam multi-stage oracle. LABELS "gpu;oracle", TIMEOUT 3600 for the reduced budget shape (mirrors jtml.oracle's convention); nightly full shape.
- Why the headless suite is untouched: the pixi test task filters `-L headless` only, so any gpu-labeled test is invisible to CI by construction; the new gpu label is additive (existing oracle tests can gain a second label "oracle;gpu" without changing `-L oracle` behavior). GPU tests run `ctest -j1` (one GPU, one runner) — serialization is the runner's job, not ctest's.
- Runner: self-hosted on the lab's existing RTX 3090 box (the U2/U6 machines named in test/CMakeLists.txt), registered with a custom gpu label, runs-on [self-hosted, gpu], nvidia-smi probe on job start; GitHub-hosted GPU runners cost ~$0.052/min (Linux 4-core) so self-hosted is the zero-marginal-cost path (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing, https://latchkey.dev/learn/ci-how-to/build-on-self-hosted-gpu-runner-github-actions). Schedule: per-PR = headless (existing) + jtml.z_profile + reduced-budget jtml.oracle_multistage; nightly = full jtml.oracle_multistage + jtml.ablation (full shape) + render smokes.
- The reduced budget shape must come from a Moré & Wild data-profile measurement, not another ad hoc number: for each candidate cumulative shape, measure the smallest total budget whose recovered pose stays above IoU ≈ 0.98 on Kneel_1, and use that for per-PR CI (https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/080724083; prior-run angle 06 finding). The existing 3600 s TIMEOUT on jtml.oracle is the smell this replaces: a gate that takes an hour is tolerated, not run.
- Gate-sensitivity companion (oracle-of-the-oracle): the 0.85 IoU gate sits far below the measured 0.9936, so we do not know what regressions trip it; the apparatus includes a perturbation suite on the gpu runner — perturb the start pose by ±1 mm/±1° per DoF and by the documented 6.31 mm z gap, break the dilation schedule, swap the variant — and assert the gate trips (checked-coverage oracle-quality practice, https://www.st.cs.uni-saarland.de/publications/files/schuler-stvr-2013.pdf). This is cheap (a handful of extra runs) and calibrates the gate's sensitivity.
- Confidence: high on the CI mechanics (labels/timeouts/registration verified in test/CMakeLists.txt + pixi.toml + workflows/cmake.yml); medium on the wall-clock estimates (no per-eval timing data for the 35k shape — the 20-60 evals/s figure is derived from the flat-3000 run's "a few minutes").
- Relevance: this closes the last gap in the measurement loop — the instruments exist (Tier-0/ablation/oracle/z-probe) AND they run on a schedule, so the measurement-first doctrine has teeth: a PR that regresses SetCallOffset bookkeeping, dilation scheduling, or z-refinement fails loudly before the algorithm work even starts.

** The z-profile probe and the multi-stage oracle both consume — never re-own — the sibling angles' outputs (non-overlap boundary)
- 02-cost-path-foundation owns the per-metric semantics tests and the 7-bug fixes with pin-first tests; the Tier-0 reference in this angle is the harness those semantics tests plug into (a test-only CPU mirror of the documented GPU metric contracts), and the Tier-2 ablation runs re-verify after 02's fixes land (bug-4's always-Trunk guard means DIRECT_DILATION_T1's paper-style path is currently unreachable — the ablation of the symmetric-vs-asymmetric dilation schedule is gated on that fix).
- 01-direct-variants specifies the variant surface (refinement control, DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate) the harness must score; this angle's ablation.json is the scoring surface, and the data-profile work is how the reduced budget is chosen.
- 05-compute-perf owns perf instrumentation (nvtx, per-eval sync removal, GPU-CI tractability numbers); this angle only sets wall-clock expectations and the gpu-label schedule, and consumes 05's per-eval timing once it exists (which will replace the derived 20-60 evals/s estimate).
- Confidence: high (boundaries are the dispatch contract, grounded in the plan-006 recommended sequence: bugs → multi-stage oracle → ablation harness)
- Relevance: prevents three angles from spec'ing the same binary three ways; the driver seam, the injected-cost lambda, and baseline.json remain the single shared vocabulary.

* What Could Not Be Verified

- The effective branch dilation at runtime: settings_constants.h implies 6/4/1 (TRUNK_DILATION 6, BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE 2 → 4, Z_SEARCH_DILATION 1) while golden_oracle.org prose says 6/3/1; the actual value is read from each CFM's registered int "Dilation" parameter at runtime and could not be verified without a running session. The ablation manifest must treat the schedule as data, not assume either value.
- Whether the tibia golden (tib.jts + Labels/tib present in example_studies/Kneel_1/Labels/tib) passes the same IoU gate — no tibia oracle run is on record; the tibia-after-femur pass of the multi-stage oracle is specified but its thresholds are uncalibrated until the first run.
- The cross-GPU IoU/L1 noise floor — only the RTX 3090 has measured numbers (0.9936 / 0.0207); the per-px L1 banded gate and any IoU threshold retune are deferred until a second GPU is measured.
- Per-eval wall-clock for the production 35k shape — no timing data exists; the 20-60 evals/s and resulting 10-30 min/frame estimates are derived from the flat-3000 run's "a few minutes" and are exactly what 05-compute-perf's instrumentation will replace.
- The per-variant z-sensitivity ranking (chamfer-heavy ≥ Mahfouz ≥ pure overlap) is a hypothesis until the z-profile probe runs; the probe is specified here precisely because the claim was never measured.
- The exact Magnification arithmetic behind the "dilated overlap is flat in z" mechanism (6.31 mm at ~1.1 m source distance → <1% scale) is derived, not measured — the probe measures the true profile directly.
- Whether the Sym_Trap manager string can be driven through OptimizerRunController today: the typed Directive enum (optimizer_run_controller_core.h:58-62) does not include it, so the tibia-ambiguity pass needs a small seam addition; the manager-side path (CalculateSymTrap at optimizer_manager.cpp:1294+) is verified, the controller-side mapping is not.
- The gate-sensitivity of IoU ≥ 0.85 (what size of regression trips it) is unknown until the perturbation suite runs — the 0.85 vs 0.9936 gap makes the gate's checked coverage an open question.

* Sources

- repo — include/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.h + src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp — OptimizerRunLaunch payload + OptimizerRunDriver interface + production adapter; the multi-stage oracle's entry point.

- repo — src/coordinator/optimizer_manager.cpp:916-1292 — the REAL stage loop (trunk 20k → 2×branch 5k → leaf 5k cumulative via SetCallOffset), per-stage re-dilate, RunDirectStage's injected-cost lambda at :1225+ (the z-profile probe entry), sym_trap_call path, non-principal (tibia) pose pinning at :937-947.
- repo — test/golden/baseline.json — authoritative budget shape (20k/25k/30k/35k), IoU 0.85 hard gate, per-px L1 0.021 informational, z 15.0 informational band, measured 0.9936/0.0207/6.31.
- repo — test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp + test/oracle/qml_parity_check.cpp — the current flat-3000 trunk-only oracle and the app-wiring parity template (frame↔label empirical pinning, backface OFF, label y-flip, IoU gate, 30-min watchdog).

#+TITLE: Measurement Apparatus — ablation runner, multi-stage oracle on the driver seam, z-profile probe, ablation.json, CI
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+PANOPTES_ANGLE: measurement-apparatus

* Summary

The measurement doctrine is already written into plan 006: *no algorithm deltas before the measurement apparatus exists* — the current oracle (test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp: 3 Kneel_1 frames, trunk-only, flat budget 3000, backface OFF, IoU ≥ 0.85) cannot see the z-weak axis, and DIRECT numeric convergence is too noisy for raw-pose gates (docs/plans/2026-08-11-006-refactor-shared-vm-layer-extraction-plan.md "Follow-On Optimization Phase"). This angle specs the apparatus in four instruments that reuse existing seams rather than new infrastructure: (1) a headless Tier-0 CPU metric reference (the per-metric semantics that 02 pins, consumed as test-only math); (2) a manifest-driven Tier-2 GPU ablation runner over the 7 registered cost variants × budget shapes × dilation schedules, writing test/golden/ablation.json; (3) a z-profile probe that sweeps z_trans through the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+) — the cheapest instrument that can see the z-weak axis; (4) a production-shaped multi-stage oracle (20k→25k→30k→35k cumulative, per-stage dilation, tibia-after-femur, sym_trap) driven through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam with appearance-only gates (per-frame IoU ≥ 0.85, per-px L1 and z recorded against baseline.json bands), plus a CI shape (new gpu label, self-hosted RTX 3090 runner, data-profile-reduced per-PR budget) that leaves the headless suite untouched.

* Key Findings

** The ablation runner is a two-tier split: a headless CPU metric reference (Tier-0) and a GPU per-variant scorer (Tier-2), joined by a manifest — never hand-written per-variant tests
- Tier-0 (headless, CI, CPU): reference implementations of the metric semantics — overlap count + comparison-white-sum normalization (FastImplantDilationMetric), mean-chamfer on the L1 distance map (DistanceMapMetric), IoU, L1,1, Mahfouz intensity ratio — on synthetic binary images, in test/unit/. The headless Frame twin already provides edge/dilation/distance-map via pure OpenCV (test/unit/frame_headless.cpp implements Canny/dilate/invert/distanceTransform against the same include/compute/frame.h), so every input the metrics consume is producible CPU-side. The metric contracts are documented in include/compute/gpu_metrics.cuh (IOU = intersection/union of white spaces; L_1_1 = summed abs diff; FastImplantDilationMetric = overlap normalized by the comparison white-pixel sum). These are test-only reference implementations (R13: no production edits); 02-cost-path-foundation owns the per-metric semantics tests and this tier consumes them.
- Tier-2 (GPU, gpu label): run each variant on Kneel_1 (3 frames) under the production budget shape with the oracle's appearance gate (silhouette IoU ≥ 0.85 vs Labels/fem — independent of all cost math; the R2 guardrail "never validate a metric by its own optimum"). Record recovered pose per axis, IoU, per-px L1, z-gap vs fem.jts, and cost-call count into ablation.json. The compute-only shape (DirectOptimizer bound to the real GPU cost, exactly oracle_test.cpp's BuildFramePipeline + cost lambda pattern) is the Tier-2 workhorse; the app-wiring shape is the multi-stage oracle below.
- Per-variant configuration surface (the matrix the manifest must encode): variant name ∈ the 7 registered costs (CostFunctionManager::listCostFunctions: sym_trap_function, DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_POLE_CONSTRAINT, DIRECT_DILATION_SAME_Z, DIRECT_DILATION_T1, DIRECT_DILATION, DIRECT_MAHFOUZ — src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423); per-stage budget shape (production 20000/5000/5000/5000 cumulative 20k→25k→30k→35k, reduced data-profile shape, flat 3000 oracle shape — baseline.json budget_per_stage/budget_cumulative_effective); per-stage dilation schedule (6/3/1 per golden_oracle.org prose vs 6/4/1 per TRUNK_DILATION 6 + BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE 2 + Z_SEARCH_DILATION 1 in include/domain/settings_constants.h — the contradiction is itself an ablation axis; each variant's own registered Dilation int param per src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp); ranges (trunk ±35, branch (15,15,25,25,25,25), leaf (3,3,15,3,3,3) — settings_constants.h); backface ON (production) vs OFF (oracle/label-generator); frame set {0,1,2}.
- Cost profile that makes this tractable: the flat-3000 oracle run takes "a few minutes" on the RTX 3090 (qml_parity_check.cpp kRunTimeoutMs = 30 min watchdog) ⇒ roughly 20–60 evals/s ⇒ the 35k production shape is ~10–30 min/frame, and the full matrix (7 variants × 3 frames × production shape) is hours — which is why the manifest is required (selectable subsets), a reduced shape is CI-default, and the full shape is nightly. [Source: repo — test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp, test/oracle/qml_parity_check.cpp:124-126, test/golden/baseline.json, src/compute/CostFunctionManager.cpp:344-423, test/unit/frame_headless.cpp, include/compute/gpu_metrics.cuh]
- Confidence: high (repo-internal, source-verified)
- Relevance to this project: this is the missing decision tool — the 7 registered variants have never been compared head-to-head (test/unit/test_cost_function.cpp covers only the parameter registry), and every algorithm claim in the run's papers (DIRECT-GLh hidden constraints, refinement control) needs this harness before it can be judged.

** The multi-stage oracle drives the REAL Optimize() stage loop through the OptimizerRunDriver seam — OptimizerRunLaunch is the payload, the controller relays are the observation channel, and the gates stay appearance-based
- The seam is ready and green: include/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.h defines OptimizerRunLaunch (calibration, camera_a/b frames, models, selected_model_indexes, primary_model_index, pose_matrix LocationStorage, OptimizerSettings, the three CostFunctionManagers by value, directive, iter_count) and the OptimizerRunDriver interface (Manager/ThreadActive/Initialize/Start/Stop/Wait) with the production adapter CreateOptimizerManagerRunDriver wrapping OptimizerManager untouched (src/coordinator/optimizer_run_driver.cpp: a fresh manager + QThread per run, finished-before-Initialize bind, H3 destructor contract). OptimizerRunController::start() drives the sequence (save-last-pose mirror → gate → seed → driver → 8 binds → Initialize → thread start) and re-emits by-value relays on the controller thread; the core exposes the oracle seam's observation channel directly: costCalls(), stageText(), progress() (optimizer_run_controller_core.h:154-165, "calls vs cumulative budget — the oracle seam, M12").
- What the oracle must therefore do: construct OptimizerRunRequest{ directive, save-last-pose mirror args, gate inputs, LocationStorage seeded from fem.jts frame 0, launch{ production OptimizerSettings, three CFMs with DIRECT_DILATION + per-stage dilation params, frames built at Canny 3/0/150 + dilation 6, models = femur (primary) + tibia (non-principal) } }, call start(), wait for runState == Completed, then run the appearance comparator (GPUModel backface OFF + GPUMetrics::IOU vs the vertically-flipped label TIFF — the exact oracle mechanics) at the pose relayed by optimizedFrameRelayed. The real stage loop runs unmodified inside OptimizerManager::Optimize(): trunk budget 20000 → 2×branch 5000 each (budget_ accumulates 25k/30k) → leaf 5000 (35k), each stage a fresh DirectOptimizer with SetCallOffset(cost_function_calls_) so the loop guard is cumulative (optimizer_manager.cpp:1031, 1087-1093, 1142-1146; DirectOptimizer::SetCallOffset in include/domain/direct_optimizer.h), per-stage re-dilate of the comparison image to the stage's dilation value, and per-stage CFM Initialize/Destruct.
- The gates (per baseline.json tolerances): (a) HARD — per-frame silhouette IoU ≥ 0.85 vs the empirically pinned label (baseline.json silhouette_iou_threshold; measured 0.9936 — the IoU gate stays the appearance arbiter, never raw pose); (b) BANDED-RECORD — per-px L1 vs the baseline 0.021 informational threshold (measured 0.0207; promote to a banded assert only after the cross-GPU noise floor is calibrated — prior-run angle 06 finding, https://www.forasoft.com/learn/video-quality/articles-vqm/regression-testing-golden-references); (c) BANDED-INFORMATIONAL — z-gap vs baseline.json pose_per_axis_informational z_tran = 15.0 (observed 6.31) — recorded per frame into ablation.json and asserted only inside the band, because DIRECT z convergence is noisy by design; (d) STAGE-BOOKKEEPING — the controller's costCalls() at each stage transition must land on the cumulative caps 20k/25k/30k/35k (± the seed eval), and per-stage CFM Dilation parameters must match the manifest — this is the regression the flat-3000 oracle is blind to (a SetCallOffset or dilation-scheduling regression passes today).
- Tibia-after-femur + sym_trap: the production workflow is sequential runs — femur as primary (tibia pinned non-principal from tib.jts via LocationStorage, which Optimize() reads for the pole/sym_trap costs at optimizer_manager.cpp:937-947), then tibia as primary with the femur pose fixed at the recovered value. The QML bridge's SingleModelOnly pre-check would reject the two-model launch, so the oracle drives OptimizerRunController directly (the widgets' full surface), not the bridge stack — qml_parity_check.cpp remains the proven harness template for the single-model case. The Sym_Trap string directive (optimizer_manager.cpp:177-185 → CalculateSymTrap) is NOT in the controller's typed Directive enum (Single/All/Each/From/… — optimizer_run_controller_core.h:58-62), so the tibia-ambiguity pass needs a small seam addition (a typed Directive::SymTrap mapped to the manager string) — the one concrete seam gap this spec found.
- Confidence: high (repo-internal, source-verified; the seam behavior is pinned by the green jtml.optimizer_run_controller lifecycle suite per the plan-006 record)
- Relevance: this is synthesis roadmap item 3 (production-shaped multi-stage oracle) — the highest-leverage expansion, and the acceptance test for any future shared-stage-loop refactor (plan 006 explicitly shapes the run controller as its future seam: "the multi-stage oracle consumes the OptimizerRunDriver seam from U5").

** The z-profile probe reuses the RunDirectStage injected-cost boundary — sweep z_trans with all other axes pinned at fem.jts truth and read the cost curve; it is the cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis
- The entry point is optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+ — RunDirectStage's injected lambda takes the denormalized physical Point6D, sets the GPU model pose (primary + biplane secondary via calibration convert), and scores stage_manager.callActiveCostFunction(). The probe replicates exactly that lambda body (or, for the driver-seam variant, drives a controller run with leaf-like settings), looping Δz ∈ {-15,-14,…,+15} mm around the fem.jts z at fixed truth for the other 5 axes, recording cost(Δz) per variant per dilation level.
- Why it exposes the z-weak-axis signal directly: the dilated-overlap family is nearly flat in z because a z shift is pure magnification — at ~1.1 m source distance a ±15 mm shift changes scale by <1%, inside the 6 px dilation tolerance — so the probe's diagnostic is the normalized depth of the cost valley: valley_depth = (max_{Δz} cost − cost(0)) / (max − min over the sweep). A healthy z signal shows a deep, centered valley; a z-blind metric shows a flat curve (or worse, an off-center one). Per-variant ranking (chamfer-heavy DIRECT_DILATION ≥ Mahfouz ≥ pure overlap) is exactly what this instrument measures — prior-run angle 01 hypothesis (repo .panoptes/jtml-research-horizons/angles/01-cost-function-landscape.org, the magnification arithmetic derived from baseline.json z_tran ≈ -1022.93 and pitch 0.373).
- Cost: 31 cost calls per (variant, dilation, frame) ≈ 31 renders — milliseconds each at ~20-60 evals/s ⇒ the whole 7-variant × 3-dilation × 3-frame probe is on the order of a couple of minutes on the RTX 3090. It needs no production changes (the boundary already exists) and no new fixtures. As a metamorphic-relation bonus it asserts cheap oracle-quality invariants: cost(0) is the sweep minimum within noise, and valley depth > a noise floor — a variant that fails this is z-blind by measurement, not by argument.
- Headless Tier-0 analog: the CPU metric reference can run the same sweep on synthetic silhouettes scaled by the magnification factor, giving a no-GPU z-sensitivity estimate; the GPU probe remains authoritative because it exercises the real render + metric path (this is 05-compute-perf's boundary: the probe consumes timing, it does not own instrumentation).
- Confidence: high on the probe mechanics (the lambda boundary is source-verified); medium on the per-variant valley-depth ranking until the probe runs (it is a measurement instrument by design, not a claim).
- Relevance: the z-weak axis is the run's load-bearing research problem (prior-run synthesis finding, converged from 5 independent literature sources + the 6.31 mm measured z gap); this probe is the instrument that turns the argument into data and gates every z remedy (SAME_Z weight calibration, chamfer reweighting, leaf refinement).

** ablation.json schema — variant × budget shape × dilation schedule × metric → per-frame IoU / per-px L1 / z-gap, plus the run hash (determinism record)
- Concrete schema (test/golden/ablation.json, sibling of baseline.json):
  #+begin_example
  {
    "schema_version": 1,
    "runner": {
      "gpu": "RTX 3090", "cuda": "12.4", "timestamp": "...",
      "run_hash": "sha256(variant|budget_shape|dilation_schedule|frames|start_pose_source|backface|edge_config)"
    },
    "variants": [
      {
        "name": "DIRECT_DILATION",
        "cost_path": "src/compute/DIRECT_DILATION.cpp",
        "params": {"Dilation": 6, "Black_Silhouette": null},
        "dilation_schedule": {"trunk": 6, "branch": 3, "leaf": 1},
        "budget_cumulative": [20000, 25000, 30000, 35000],
        "ranges": {"trunk": [35,35,35,35,35,35], "branch": [15,15,25,25,25,25], "leaf": [3,3,15,3,3,3]},
        "backface": false,
        "edge_config": {"canny": [3, 0, 150]},
        "results": [
          {"frame": 0, "recovered_pose": [x,y,z,xa,ya,za],
           "iou": 0.9936, "l1_per_px": 0.0207, "z_gap_mm": 6.31,
           "cost_calls": 35000, "elapsed_s": 1234.0,
           "gate": {"iou_pass": true, "l1_band_pass": true, "z_band_pass": true}}
        ],
        "determinism": {"seeds": [], "note": "no RNG in DIRECT or the int-atomic cost path; run_hash is the determinism twin",
                        "re_runs_identical": true}
      }
    ],
    "z_profiles": [
      {"variant": "DIRECT_DILATION", "dilation": 6, "frame": 0,
       "sweep_mm": [-15,-14,...,15], "costs": [ ... ],
       "valley_depth_norm": 0.42, "argmin_mm": 1.0}
    ]
  }
  #+end_example
- Determinism semantics (the seeds column is honest about being empty today): DIRECT is RNG-free (pure convex-hull/trisection bookkeeping — src/domain/direct_optimizer.cpp) and every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd, which is order-independent and therefore value-deterministic run-to-run on a machine (prior-run angle 05 finding; the only float-atomic reduction, render_drr_engine.cu's DRR fill, is not in the DIRECT cost path). So the determinism twin is: same run_hash ⇒ bit-identical output on the same GPU; the runner asserts it by running the flagship variant twice. The seeds array is reserved for future stochastic variants (e.g., multistart) and for cross-GPU noise-floor trials.
- The run_hash (not a seed) is the schema's regression tripwire: any change to variant/budget/dilation/frame-set/start-pose-source/backface/edge-config that forgets to update the manifest changes the hash and fails the diff review.
- Confidence: high (schema is a proposal grounded in the verified repo fields: baseline.json's budget_cumulative_effective/tolerances/measured block is the template; the 7 variants' registered params are source-verified)
- Relevance: ablation.json is the decision record the harness produces — the per-variant z-gap table is what the DIRECT variant switch (01-direct-variants) and the weight calibrations (02) get judged against; it lives next to baseline.json so the golden spec and the ablation data are one directory.

** CI integration — a new gpu ctest label, a self-hosted RTX 3090 runner, a data-profile-reduced per-PR budget shape, and nightly full shape; the headless suite is untouched by construction
- Current state: the headless suite is `ctest -L headless` (pixi.toml test task, --timeout 600) and is the only thing GitHub Actions runs (workflows/cmake.yml); GPU tests carry labels "oracle" (TIMEOUT 3600) and "oracle;render" (TIMEOUT 120) and are never in the default run — the split is already load-bearing. New tests must follow the same registration recipe (repo-root WORKING_DIRECTORY, xcb env for renderers, explicit labels).
- New targets and labels:
  - jtml.metric_reference — Tier-0 CPU metric reference + z-profile Tier-0 analog. LABELS "headless", TIMEOUT 120-300. Zero GPU, zero impact on the existing 46 headless tests beyond a new green target.
  - jtml.z_profile — GPU probe. LABELS "gpu;oracle", TIMEOUT 600 (a couple of minutes of renders). This is the per-PR z-health check.
  - jtml.ablation — manifest-driven runner. LABELS "gpu", TIMEOUT sized to the manifest's budget shape (reduced shape ≤ 30 min per PR; the full production shape is NOT a ctest case — it is a nightly job with a job-level timeout, because 7 variants × 3 frames × 35k evals is hours).
  - jtml.oracle_multistage — the driver-seam multi-stage oracle. LABELS "gpu;oracle", TIMEOUT 3600 for the reduced budget shape (mirrors jtml.oracle's convention); nightly full shape.
- Why the headless suite is untouched: the pixi test task filters `-L headless` only, so any gpu-labeled test is invisible to CI by construction; the new gpu label is additive (existing oracle tests can gain a second label "oracle;gpu" without changing `-L oracle` behavior). GPU tests run `ctest -j1` (one GPU, one runner) — serialization is the runner's job, not ctest's.
- Runner: self-hosted on the lab's existing RTX 3090 box (the U2/U6 machines named in test/CMakeLists.txt), registered with a custom gpu label, runs-on [self-hosted, gpu], nvidia-smi probe on job start; GitHub-hosted GPU runners cost ~$0.052/min (Linux 4-core) so self-hosted is the zero-marginal-cost path (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing, https://latchkey.dev/learn/ci-how-to/build-on-self-hosted-gpu-runner-github-actions). Schedule: per-PR = headless (existing) + jtml.z_profile + reduced-budget jtml.oracle_multistage; nightly = full jtml.oracle_multistage + jtml.ablation (full shape) + render smokes.
- The reduced budget shape must come from a Moré & Wild data-profile measurement, not another ad hoc number: for each candidate cumulative shape, measure the smallest total budget whose recovered pose stays above IoU ≈ 0.98 on Kneel_1, and use that for per-PR CI (https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/080724083; prior-run angle 06 finding). The existing 3600 s TIMEOUT on jtml.oracle is the smell this replaces: a gate that takes an hour is tolerated, not run.
- Gate-sensitivity companion (oracle-of-the-oracle): the 0.85 IoU gate sits far below the measured 0.9936, so we do not know what regressions trip it; the apparatus includes a perturbation suite on the gpu runner — perturb the start pose by ±1 mm/±1° per DoF and by the documented 6.31 mm z gap, break the dilation schedule, swap the variant — and assert the gate trips (checked-coverage oracle-quality practice, https://www.st.cs.uni-saarland.de/publications/files/schuler-stvr-2013.pdf). This is cheap (a handful of extra runs) and calibrates the gate's sensitivity.
- Confidence: high on the CI mechanics (labels/timeouts/registration verified in test/CMakeLists.txt + pixi.toml + workflows/cmake.yml); medium on the wall-clock estimates (no per-eval timing data for the 35k shape — the 20-60 evals/s figure is derived from the flat-3000 run's "a few minutes").
- Relevance: this closes the last gap in the measurement loop — the instruments exist (Tier-0/ablation/oracle/z-probe) AND they run on a schedule, so the measurement-first doctrine has teeth: a PR that regresses SetCallOffset bookkeeping, dilation scheduling, or z-refinement fails loudly before the algorithm work even starts.

** The z-profile probe and the multi-stage oracle both consume — never re-own — the sibling angles' outputs (non-overlap boundary)
- 02-cost-path-foundation owns the per-metric semantics tests and the 7-bug fixes with pin-first tests; the Tier-0 reference in this angle is the harness those semantics tests plug into (a test-only CPU mirror of the documented GPU metric contracts), and the Tier-2 ablation runs re-verify after 02's fixes land (bug-4's always-Trunk guard means DIRECT_DILATION_T1's paper-style path is currently unreachable — the ablation of the symmetric-vs-asymmetric dilation schedule is gated on that fix).
- 01-direct-variants specifies the variant surface (refinement control, DIRECT-GLh hidden-constraint surrogate) the harness must score; this angle's ablation.json is the scoring surface, and the data-profile work is how the reduced budget is chosen.
- 05-compute-perf owns perf instrumentation (nvtx, per-eval sync removal, GPU-CI tractability numbers); this angle only sets wall-clock expectations and the gpu-label schedule, and consumes 05's per-eval timing once it exists (which will replace the derived 20-60 evals/s estimate).
- Confidence: high (boundaries are the dispatch contract, grounded in the plan-006 recommended sequence: bugs → multi-stage oracle → ablation harness)
- Relevance: prevents three angles from spec'ing the same binary three ways; the driver seam, the injected-cost lambda, and baseline.json remain the single shared vocabulary.

* What Could Not Be Verified

- The effective branch dilation at runtime: settings_constants.h implies 6/4/1 (TRUNK_DILATION 6, BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE 2 → 4, Z_SEARCH_DILATION 1) while golden_oracle.org prose says 6/3/1; the actual value is read from each CFM's registered int "Dilation" parameter at runtime and could not be verified without a running session. The ablation manifest must treat the schedule as data, not assume either value.
- Whether the tibia golden (tib.jts + Labels/tib present in example_studies/Kneel_1/Labels/tib) passes the same IoU gate — no tibia oracle run is on record; the tibia-after-femur pass of the multi-stage oracle is specified but its thresholds are uncalibrated until the first run.
- The cross-GPU IoU/L1 noise floor — only the RTX 3090 has measured numbers (0.9936 / 0.0207); the per-px L1 banded gate and any IoU threshold retune are deferred until a second GPU is measured.
- Per-eval wall-clock for the production 35k shape — no timing data exists; the 20-60 evals/s and resulting 10-30 min/frame estimates are derived from the flat-3000 run's "a few minutes" and are exactly what 05-compute-perf's instrumentation will replace.
- The per-variant z-sensitivity ranking (chamfer-heavy ≥ Mahfouz ≥ pure overlap) is a hypothesis until the z-profile probe runs; the probe is specified here precisely because the claim was never measured.
- The exact Magnification arithmetic behind the "dilated overlap is flat in z" mechanism (6.31 mm at ~1.1 m source distance → <1% scale) is derived, not measured — the probe measures the true profile directly.
- Whether the Sym_Trap manager string can be driven through OptimizerRunController today: the typed Directive enum (optimizer_run_controller_core.h:58-62) does not include it, so the tibia-ambiguity pass needs a small seam addition; the manager-side path (CalculateSymTrap at optimizer_manager.cpp:1294+) is verified, the controller-side mapping is not.
- The gate-sensitivity of IoU ≥ 0.85 (what size of regression trips it) is unknown until the perturbation suite runs — the 0.85 vs 0.9936 gap makes the gate's checked coverage an open question.

* Sources

- repo — test/oracle/oracle_test.cpp + test/oracle/qml_parity_check.cpp — the current flat-3000 trunk-only oracle and the app-wiring parity template (frame↔label empirical pinning, backface OFF, label y-flip, IoU gate, 30-min watchdog).

#+TITLE: Panoptes Research: Optimizer Deep-Dive — Architecture + Algorithm Upgrades
#+DATE: 2026-08-12
#+RESEARCH_ANGLES: 6
#+STATUS: complete

* Executive Summary

The single highest-leverage finding of this run: **the current 0.9936 IoU baseline is measured against a deterministically-corrupted cost term.** Angle 02 verified at the dispatch's line numbers that the distance-map index formula (distance_map_metric.cu:27, `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` instead of `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`) mis-maps every block row, so the distance-map term of every DIRECT_DILATION oracle evaluation accumulates at the wrong pixels. That is the one live bug of the seven verified — the other six poison latent paths only. Fixing it and re-baselining (one single re-baseline after all behavior-neutral fixes land) is the prerequisite for every other decision in this run: variant switches, perf cuts, and gradient polish are all judged against a baseline that is not trustworthy until this lands. The gate (IoU ≥ 0.85) is far below the measured 0.9936, so the appearance arbiter stays, but measured IoU / per-px L1 / the 6.31 mm z gap are informational and expected to move.

The recommended course of action, in dependency order: (1) pin-first fixes per angle 02 (Tier-0 pins, then behavior-neutral fixes, then the distance-map index fix + one oracle re-baseline); (2) the measurement apparatus per angle 03 — the z-profile probe on the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis) and the production-shaped multi-stage oracle through the plan-006 OptimizerRunDriver seam; (3) the ablation runner + ablation.json as the scoring surface; (4) the evidence-backed algorithm upgrade from angle 01 — **1-DTC-GL-gb** (GL two-step Pareto selection + globally-biased refinement control), scored by the harness before any production switch; (5) compute-perf cuts 0–4 per angle 05, gated on oracle green and bit-identical cost values; (6) the differentiable-polish stage per angle 06, GO-gated on the z-profile probe and an ablation arm. Architecture work (angle 04) is the enabler that flows through this path as additive cuts A–E rather than a separate project.

Two tensions the user should carry explicitly. First, **the variant switch cannot fix the z-axis**: angle 01's GL recommendation improves search efficiency in 6-D at n>4 budgets (≈60–72% fewer evaluations, high-evidence), but angle 06 shows the 6.31 mm z gap is a magnification observability limit in single-plane fluoro — no selection/partitioning scheme changes what is observable, and a depth channel does not fix it either; the real z remedies are biplane (already supported) or a known-geometry prior, and every z remedy is gated on angle 03's probe. Second, **perf cuts do not sacrifice determinism**: angle 05 verified every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd (order-independent, value-deterministic), so async copies and iteration batching can preserve bit-identical results — the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim applies to the DRR float-atomic path, which is not in the DIRECT cost path; a pose→score diff harness makes the bit-identity claim checkable per cut.

The "12x fewer evals" polish thesis should be treated as a target to test, not a justification: angle 06's analysis puts the realistic win at ~1.5–3× in the leaf/refinement phase (trunk 20k dominates the budget), with the chamfer distance-map surrogate as the one smooth gradient signal that exists in the codebase. Everything else from the papers — DIRECT-GLh hidden constraints, 1-DTDV boundary sampling, analytic-AA occlusion gradients, DRR-photometric gradients, torch bridges — is conditional, deferred, or NO-GO per the evidence below, and each lands only through the harness.

* Key Findings

** Finding 1 — The baseline is contaminated by a live kernel bug; one re-baseline is the run's critical path
- Angle 02 verified all 7 cost-path bugs at the dispatch's line numbers. Only one is live in the oracle's cost (DIRECT_DILATION): the grid→pixel index formula at distance_map_metric.cu:27 uses `blockIdx.y + gridDim.x` where the correct formula is `blockIdx.y * gridDim.x`. For the 64×64 crop / 16×16-block case: crop rows 0–15 are never visited, rows 20–23 are visited twice; the metric is deterministic but wrong. The IoU 0.9936 / per-px L1 0.0207 / z gap 6.31 mm baseline therefore includes this corruption in every evaluation. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Bug 5]
- The six other bugs are dead for the oracle: uninitialized min_dist (DD_NEW_POLE_CONSTRAINT.cpp:134, UB read — can be a signalling NaN), Y_dist ≡ X_dist no-op (117–120), sym_trap tibia x→z (sym_trap_function.cpp:106), always-Trunk stage guard (CostFunctionManager.cpp:46 — tautology, makes DIRECT_DILATION_T1's branch/leaf behavior unreachable), Mahfouz pointer-guard + int truncation (implant_mahfouz_metric.cu:324/446, :93/122), curvature stub returning 0 + per-stage allocation leak. A dead duplicate DistanceMapMetric call sits commented at DIRECT_DILATION.cpp:101–104. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Bugs 1–4, 6–7]
- Pin-first recipes exist for every bug: Tier-0 pure-surface pins (extracted helpers, CPU references) where a pure surface exists, Tier-2 GPU-labeled pins where the pin must observe the cost itself. All pins are red or spec-documenting today — that is the R13 characterization pass, and it creates the pure surfaces the fixes plug into. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, "Fix order"]
- Execution consequence: fix all behavior-neutral bugs first (zero oracle impact), then the distance-map index fix, then a single oracle re-run and baseline.json re-baseline. Only one re-baseline happens. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, Phase 0–2]
- Cross-reference: angle 06 explicitly warns new polish kernels must NOT copy the buggy index formula; angle 03's Tier-0 metric references must encode the corrected formula as spec. All three angles converge on the same critical path. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, Tier-0 section]

** Finding 2 — Measurement-first is unanimous across all six angles: no algorithm delta before the apparatus
- The doctrine (plan 006: "no algorithm deltas before the measurement apparatus exists") is independently restated by every angle as its ordering rule: 01 "no variant touches production until the harness says so"; 03 is the apparatus spec itself; 04's cuts A–E are each pin-gated; 05 gates every perf cut on oracle green + bit-identity; 06 ships polish behind enable_polish_ and lands it only when the ablation arm wins at equal-or-lower cumulative budget. This is converged evidence, not a single source. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, 03-measurement-apparatus.org, 04-backend-architecture.org, 05-compute-perf.org, 06-differentiable-polish.org]
- The current oracle cannot see what needs measuring: 3 frames, trunk-only, flat budget 3000, backface OFF — NOT the production shape, leaf z-refinement never exercised by any test, and a SetCallOffset or dilation-scheduling regression passes today. The multi-stage oracle (20k→25k→30k→35k cumulative, per-stage dilation, tibia-after-femur, sym_trap) driven through the OptimizerRunDriver seam closes that gap, with a stage-bookkeeping gate (costCalls() must land on 20k/25k/30k/35k) that the flat oracle is blind to. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "multi-stage oracle"]
- The driver seam is ready and green: OptimizerRunLaunch (by-value payload incl. 3 CostFunctionManagers), the OptimizerRunDriver interface, CreateOptimizerManagerRunDriver wrapping OptimizerManager untouched, and the controller's by-value relays (optimizedFrameRelayed) plus the oracle observation channel (costCalls/stageText/progress — "the oracle seam, M12"). One concrete seam gap was found: the typed Directive enum lacks SymTrap (needed for the tibia-ambiguity pass); a small seam addition is required. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "multi-stage oracle"; local-recon.org]
- The ablation matrix must encode: 7 registered variants × budget shapes (production 20/25/30/35k, reduced CI shape, flat-3000 oracle shape) × dilation schedules (6/3/1 vs 6/4/1 — itself an ablation axis) × backface ON/OFF × frames {0,1,2}. Cost profile: flat-3000 is "a few minutes" → ~20–60 evals/s → full 35k production shape ~10–30 min/frame → full matrix is hours, hence manifest-driven subsets: reduced shape per-PR, full shape nightly. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "ablation runner", "CI integration"]

** Finding 3 — The literature's highest-evidence algorithm upgrade is 1-DTC-GL-gb, and the current config is the literature's worst local-refinement regime
- Current repo config: original-DIRECT selection, ε=0, selecting ALL hull ties, 1-DTC-alike trisection on the largest denormalized side, L2 size measure. Jones & Martins 2021: ε=0 "spends so many evaluations refining local minima"; the empirical study: tie-all selection increases "global drag". The repo sits exactly in the worst regime the literature documents for a 20k–35k budget. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07150; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912]
- GL (two-step Pareto) selection beats IO/IA by ~60–72% on n>4 problems; budget crossover: IO wins ≤500 evals, N-DTC-IO best ~1000–4000, GL best ≥4000 — the 6-DOF search at 20k trunk lives far above the crossover. Partitioning: 1-DBDP best n>4 average but needs diagonal-bisection rework; 1-DTC best GKLS median and minimal code change; 1-DTDV catastrophic for interior optima (141,999 evals vs 919 on Levy10) — a trap unless the pose optimum is confirmed near the range boundary. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 2; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.14912 §4.1–4.2, Table 3]
- Refinement control (Mathematics 2022, 10, 3760): every restriction except -gb hurts 1-DTC-GL on 287 DIRECTGOLib problems; -gb is the only one that never hurt and is best on expensive objectives (GPU silhouette with dilation 6/4/1 renders is expensive). Restrictions hurt worst when f* ≈ 0 — the silhouette-cost shape. ε-style restrictions are doubly contraindicated (the ε|f_min| window collapses as f_min→0). Landing variant: **1-DTC-GL-gb**, ε=0, L2 size kept, bit-identical defaults preserved behind an Options struct. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 4; https://epublications.vu.lt/object/elaba:143490244/143490244.pdf §3–§4]
- DIRECT-GLh (φ = f_min + d(x_min,x) surrogate for infeasible/NaN points) is near-zero cost — the distances are already computed by GL's two-step selection — and beats barrier/NAS methods 18/80 vs 29–53/80 failures on hidden-constraint problems. But the trigger is unverified: no finite-check exists anywhere in the C++ cost path, so whether the production GPU cost can emit NaN is unknown; angle 02's cost-path audit owns that check, and GLh is conditional on it. Today a NaN result poisons hull slope comparisons in ConvexHull (silent storage corruption). [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, Finding 3; https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02205 §2.3, §4.2.1]

** Finding 4 — The z-weak axis is an observability limit, not an algorithm problem; the probe is the arbiter, and the real remedies are biplane or a known-geometry prior
- The 6.31 mm z gap (vs 0.16/0.08 in-plane) is the run's load-bearing research problem, converged from prior runs. The mechanism: a z shift is pure magnification — at ~1.1 m source distance a ±15 mm shift changes scale by <1%, inside the 6 px dilation tolerance; the dilated-overlap family is nearly flat in z. [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "z-profile probe"; local-recon.org]
- The z-profile probe reuses the RunDirectStage injected-cost lambda (optimizer_manager.cpp:1225+): sweep Δz ∈ {−15,…,+15} mm at fixed truth for the other 5 axes, 31 cost calls per (variant, dilation, frame) — a couple of minutes total on the RTX 3090 — and report valley_depth = (max−cost(0))/(max−min). A z-blind metric shows a flat or off-center curve. This is the cheapest instrument that sees the z-weak axis, and it gates every z remedy (SAME_Z weight calibration, chamfer reweighting, leaf refinement). [Source: angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "z-profile probe"]
- Angle 06's verdict on the depth channel: the machinery is ~80% present (DRR fill already interpolates perspective-correct z; dev_z_line_values_ buffer exists), but a front-surface z/w buffer does NOT make z observable in single-plane fluoro — there is no target depth to compare against, the gap is the magnification limit (no gradient changes what is observable), and NVDiffrast intentionally does not backprop through z/w (issue #70). The depth machinery is worth it only as: occlusion-aware visibility gradients, a synthetic-depth loss in the harness's self-supervised arm, or the z-line-integral in the ML/DRR pathway. The real z fixes are biplane (calibration_.convert_Pose_A_to_Pose_B + biplane branch already exist) and the known-geometry prior (implant constrained to a registered bone) — matching the prior-run ML angle's finding 8. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "depth channel"; https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/issues/70]
- This is the dispatch-requested contradiction flag: angle 01's variant recommendations (1-DTC-GL-gb) optimize search efficiency but cannot move the z gap — the two are different kinds of improvement, and the probe is the instrument that separates them. A variant-switch win on the harness must not be mistaken for a z fix.

** Finding 5 — The cost path is sync-bound (structurally confirmed, magnitude unmeasured); 3 of 5 D2H syncs are trivially async-able, and int-atomics make bit-identical results achievable
- Per monoplane eval: ~15 kernel launches (8 render + 4 fast-implant-dilation + 3 distance-map) + 5 synchronous D2H cudaMemcpy, all on the default stream, zero streams/events anywhere in src/. The 5 syncs classify as: 2 structural mid-eval (bounding box at render_engine.cu:781–785; fragment_fill at :786–790 — removable only via kernel-level change) and 3 terminal (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:289–290; distance_map_metric.cu:110–114, :115–119) — async-able now, all targets already page-locked. Cost nuance: the pairs share drains, so the real exposure is ~3 host-block windows per eval. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Sync-point inventory"]
- The existing ms/call meter (optimizer_manager.cpp:1272–1278) uses clock() = process CPU time: it excludes GPU time AND sync-wait time, so it systematically under-reads a sync-bound pipeline and cannot arbitrate the item-8 claim. Fixing the meter (Cut 4) is required before any cut can be demonstrated to the user via the UI. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The ms/call meter"]
- Determinism: every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd/atomicSub on single counters — integer addition is order-independent, so identical launch configs + inputs ⇒ bit-identical scores. This resolves the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim: it applies to the DRR float-atomic path, which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Consequence: async terminal copies and iteration batching can be verified bit-identical by diffing a recorded pose→score sequence; Cut 3 (fragment-fill removal) must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Determinism"]
- The DIRECT loop is sequential but each iteration's evals are pairwise independent (TrisectPotentiallyOptimal evaluates 2×N centers from a pre-loop snapshot) — batchable with replay-ordered bookkeeping, no GPU kernel rewrite. Constraint: FastImplantDilationMetric writes INTO the rendered buffer, so evals must be double-buffered (second render output + duplicate score buffers); biplane gets a free overlap (secondary camera buffers are separate). [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "The DIRECT loop is sequential", "In-place metric composition"]
- nvtx: declared in pixi.toml, zero instrumentation, and -DLIBNVTOOLSEXT is dead config; the nvtx3 header-only API compiles with no CMake/link change (toolkit include path already on jtml_compute). nsight-compute is in the lock; nsight-systems is not (needs pixi add). Per-eval timing data from Cut 0 replaces angle 03's derived 20–60 evals/s estimate. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "nvtx", "Measurement protocol"]

** Finding 6 — The polish stage is feasible only on a smooth surrogate; GO for chamfer-gradient polish, NO-GO for photometric/torch routes; the "12x" thesis is likely overstated
- The production DIRECT_DILATION cost is piecewise-constant in pose (binary silhouette + int reductions): finite differences on it give zero/garbage Jacobians; there is no gradient to polish through it. The surrogate already exists: DistanceMapMetric is a mean-chamfer loss with a Lipschitz image-space gradient ∇D, and its analytic gradient is the standard silhouette gradient dL/dθ = Σ ∇D(p)·(dp/dθ), needing only the per-pixel triangle-ID + barycentrics FillTriangleKernel already computes and discards (~10 lines + one float4 buffer to stage them). Published relatives: arXiv:1906.07870, arXiv:2501.14918. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "piecewise-constant", "smooth surrogate"]
- Feasibility verdicts: silhouette-gradient polish on the chamfer surrogate — GO (MVP = forward differences, 6 renders/step ~1 week; then analytic Jacobian + ∇D kernel, 1 render/step, +1 week; reuses Render(), uploaded distance maps, injected-cost lambda; float accumulation; match production backface=true and leaf dilation 1). NDC z/w depth buffer — feasible machinery but NOT a z fix; only as occlusion/ablation enabler. Analytic AA / occlusion-aware gradients — research increment after the MVP shows a win. Photometric DRR-intensity gradient — NO-GO for now (+3–6 weeks, low expected value). Finite-difference on the production cost — NO-GO. Torch bridge — NO-GO on design merit (autograd buys nothing for a 6-DoF static-STL scatter-add backward; and torch is already linked into jtml_compute — the ATen include in CostFunctionManager.h is a smell flagged to angle 04). [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"]
- Hybrid loop: trunk 20k → 2×branch 5k → leaf 5k → RunPolishStage(current_optimum) → optional DIRECT re-seed around the polished pose (Gablonsky locally-biased DIRECT / DIRECT+DF-local-search literature). Plug-in point mirrors RunDirectStage, no OptimizerRunLaunch signature change (reuses the leaf CostFunctionManager), budget-accounted (every surrogate + verification eval increments cost_function_calls_ so DIRECT-only vs DIRECT+polish is apples-to-apples at equal cumulative budget). Deliberately NOT routed through the Stage enum — the always-Trunk guard bug makes it unreliable. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "hybrid loop"]
- The "~12x fewer evals" thesis: unverified and structurally suspect — the budget is trunk-dominated (20k of 35k), so a 12x total claim requires shrinking the trunk (the ML-initializer pathway's job), while a gradient method plausibly converges the leaf refinement (~10^2 steps on a smooth surrogate) several-fold faster. Realistic expectation to measure: ~1.5–3× on the leaf phase + tighter final accuracy + lower frame-to-frame variance, at equal cumulative budget, reported data-profile style. GO condition for production: ablation arm shows ≥ the IoU gate at equal-or-lower cumulative budget with no per-axis regression; precondition: the z-profile probe shows the chamfer surrogate's valley is deeper than the dilated-overlap valley. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "12x thesis", "go/no-go"]

** Finding 7 — The backend seam evolution is additive-first and deliberately minimal: payload + StageScript + named derivations, no new layer
- The "backend" is already a stack of three seams (OptimizerRunDriver, Optimize()'s stage loop, DirectOptimizer's injected std::function). The target shape: OptimizerRunLaunch stays the single by-value payload, additively gaining the DIRECT Options struct; the stage sequence becomes a StageScript (vector of StageSpec: {kind, range, budget, repeat, cfm_index}) that the same Optimize() executor consumes; dilation/dark-silhouette derivation (DeriveStageCostParams) and the cost-adapter construction (BuildGpuCostAdapter) become named pure functions; DirectOptimizer's boundary stays std::function<double(const Point6D&)>. Explicitly NO RunBackend enum (the driver IS the run-level backend — the fake driver proves it), NO new CMake target, NO headless executor extraction until the multi-stage oracle demonstrates the driver seam insufficient, NO ML in the loop. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Target shape", "non-goals"]
- Dilation stays COST-owned: it is a derived property of the active CFM parameters (the "Dilation"/"dark_silhouette" name scan at optimizer_manager.cpp:237–345), not optimizer config — moving it would fork the single source of truth. The seam is the named pure function DeriveStageCostParams, called once in Initialize. This deliberately counters the dispatch's "dilation under optimizer configuration" framing. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Dilation stays COST-owned"]
- Payload evolution contract: additive fields are FREE (DirectOptimizer::Options defaulted = today's behavior; the fake-driver test records the whole launch by value and compiles unchanged); restructuring into nested sections is ONE gated signature-adaptation cut with the test updated in the same change; the driver interface, Initialize signature, by-value forwarding, the 8 binds, and the epoch/threadActive gate never change. Do NOT move the 3 CFMs to pointers (perf decision pending measurement; would change the fake-driver copy semantics). [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "Payload evolution contract"]
- The stage loop stays in Optimize() and becomes script-driven in place: the loop is the only algorithm policy among three interleaved work kinds (session/GPU state and signal emission stay in the manager). RunDirectStage stays the stage runner; its injected lambda becomes BuildGpuCostAdapter, with three consumers converging on it (production runner, z-profile probe, and oracle_test's hand-rolled twin at oracle_test.cpp:286–291). A future gradient-polish stage is one StageSpec + one new StageKind + its own runner branch — same seam, no StageRunner interface built today. R13 gap honestly recorded: Optimize()'s loop has no headless emission-order pin today (manager is GPU-bound); Cut B's evidence is parity + oracle green + jj diff relocation + the new pure-function pins. [Source: angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "script-driven loop", "R13 pin surface", "Migration sketch"]

- Angle 02 resolved this with source evidence: the code implements 6/4/1 — settings_control.cpp:1201–1206 sets branch=4, leaf=1; settings_constants.h TRUNK_DILATION=6 / BRANCH_DILATION_DECREASE=2 / Z_SEARCH_DILATION=1 agree (consumed only by the experimental SettingsBridge); production OptimizerManager reads the per-manager "Dilation" runtime parameter. The 6/3/1 claim lives only in golden_oracle.org prose + baseline.json. Both agree on trunk 6 and leaf 1; the conflict is branch only (4 vs 3). Neither was ever runtime-captured (the flat-3000 oracle never exercises branch/leaf). Evidence favors 6/4/1 as implemented intent; docs are the stale artifact. Angle 03 treats the schedule as an ablation axis (data, not assumption); angle 04 requires DeriveStageCostParams to return exactly what the manager derives today. Resolution path: Tier-0 registry/constants pins → runtime probe → update golden_oracle.org + baseline.json to 6/4/1 or change settings_control.cpp:1204 to 3. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, "Dilation 6/4/1 vs 6/3/1"; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "ablation runner"; angles/04-backend-architecture.org, "What Could Not Be Verified"]

** Contradiction 2 — Variant recommendations (angle 01) vs the z-axis (angles 03/06)
- Not a factual disagreement but a scoping tension the user must hold: angle 01's GL/1-DTC-GL-gb upgrade is about search efficiency at n>4, ≥4000-eval budgets — it changes which poses are tried, not what the cost can observe. The z gap is an observability limit (magnification, <1% scale change over ±15 mm at ~1.1 m). No selection/partitioning scheme, and no depth channel, changes that; the probe (angle 03) is the instrument that arbitrates, and the real z remedies are biplane/prior (angle 06). Do not read a harness win from the variant switch as evidence the z problem is addressed. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org]

** Contradiction 3 — Perf cuts vs determinism: the docs' "atomics aren't bit-reproducible" claim vs the verified int-atomic cost path
- Angle 05 verified every active cost-path reduction is an int atomicAdd/atomicSub (fast_implant_dilation_metric.cu:145,147; distance_map_metric.cu:46–47; gpu_metrics.cu:129; iou.cu:66–72) — integer addition is order-independent, so results ARE bit-reproducible given identical launch configs and inputs. The order-nondeterministic float atomicAdd lives in the DRR fill (render_drr_engine.cu), which is NOT in the DIRECT cost path. Resolution: the docs' claim is stale; the determinism twin is a pose→score diff harness, and every perf cut (async copies, batching) is gated on the diff being empty. The one cut with a real determinism caveat is Cut 3 (fragment-fill kernel change), which must preserve per-thread work for threads < fragment_fill exactly. [Source: angles/05-compute-perf.org, "Determinism"; angles/03-measurement-apparatus.org, "ablation.json — determinism semantics"]

** Contradiction 4 — Backface culling: production ON vs oracle/label-generator OFF
- Production OptimizerManager constructs GPUModel with use_backface_culling=true; every oracle/parity path and the Study2Grid label generator use false (in-source comment: "BACKFACE CULLING APPEARS TO BE GIVING ERRORS"). The oracle must stay OFF: labels were generated OFF, and the frame↔label correspondence is pinned empirically by start-pose render IoU == 1.0 only under OFF; switching the oracle would break the gate against OFF-generated labels. The measured 0.9936 is an OFF-vs-OFF number and self-consistent. For production, ON is defensible for a closed opaque implant, but the two paths render different silhouette conventions where the STL is open/concave. Recommended evidence before touching production: (a) headless manifoldness check on KR_right_7_fem.stl (boundary edges == 0 ⇒ closed), (b) GPU-labeled ON-vs-OFF silhouette IoU at the golden pose (≈1.0 ⇒ immaterial; measurably <1 ⇒ deliberate reconciliation needed). Angle 06's polish must match the production backface config (true) for verification consistency — itself a tension with the oracle's OFF pin. [Source: angles/02-cost-path-foundation.org, "Backface divergence"; angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"]

** Contradiction 5 — Torch in the cost path: linked-but-banned
- torch is already linked into jtml_compute (machine_learning_tools.cpp is in the lib; CostFunctionManager.h includes <ATen/ops/div_native.h>) yet angle 06 says NO-GO on a torch bridge for polish (autograd buys nothing for the scatter-add backward; violates the "no torch in the cost path" design). The objection is design/convention, not dependency cost. The ATen include is a smell flagged to angle 04's architecture session. This is a latent inconsistency in the codebase, not a disagreement between angles. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "Feasibility verdicts"; angles/04-backend-architecture.org]

** Contradiction 6 — "12x fewer evals" (user's thesis) vs angle 06's ~1.5–3× leaf-phase estimate
- The thesis is unverified and structurally implausible as a total-budget claim: the trunk (20k of 35k cumulative) dominates, and polish cannot shrink the global phase. The honest target: evals-to-target-IoU at equal cumulative budget, data-profile style, with the win concentrated in leaf refinement. This is not a dispute about facts — it is the run's one explicitly low-confidence claim, to be arbitrated by the ablation arm. [Source: angles/06-differentiable-polish.org, "12x thesis"]

** Contradiction 7 — Split tie-break: repo (largest denormalized side) vs study (least-split-so-far)
- Angle 01: the repo's 1-DTC-alike rule ties break on the denormalized side length; the 2022 study's 1-DTC ties break least-split-so-far then lowest index. For anisotropic branch/leaf ranges (15,15,25,25,25,25; 3,3,15,3,3,3) the rules diverge; the effect on the 6-DOF search is unquantified. The battery should include an anisotropic-range probe using the actual trunk/branch/leaf ranges as box bounds. This is a mechanical-difference flag, not a correctness dispute — the repo's behavior is the pinned baseline either way. [Source: angles/01-direct-variants.org, "Partitioning schemes", "What Could Not Be Verified"]
